FMCSA DRUG AND ALCOHOL CLEARINGHOUSE PRE-EMPLOYMENT QUERY — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme Trucking, Inc.

ABOUT THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes the federal Commercial Driver's License Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse — a database maintained by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) under 49 CFR Part 382, Subpart G — and the pre-employment and annual query duties that Subpart G places on an employer of a commercial motor vehicle driver, in connection with Acme Trucking, Inc.'s employment or prospective employment of Jordan Lee in the position of Commercial Driver. This is a federal regulatory framework, not a California statute; it applies regardless of state to an employer and driver within its coverage. It is separate from, and does not replace, this corpus's other driver-related documents — the DMV Employer Pull Notice Program (a California driving-record system) and the Transportation Network Company Driver Background Check Requirements (California's rideshare-specific screening statute) — because the Clearinghouse addresses a different subject: a driver's own record of verified drug and alcohol testing violations under the federal testing rules, not a driving record or a rideshare-specific criminal background check. This sheet does not itself query the Clearinghouse, does not determine whether Jordan Lee's position in fact requires a commercial driver's license or otherwise falls within Part 382's coverage, and does not tell Acme Trucking, Inc. or Jordan Lee what to do about any particular query result.

WHO PART 382 COVERS
The Clearinghouse query duties described in this document arise under 49 CFR Part 382, and Part 382 states its own coverage in terms of a driver's licensing requirement rather than a job title: it applies to every person, and to all employers of such persons, who operate a commercial motor vehicle in commerce in any state and are subject to the commercial driver's license requirements of 49 CFR Part 383 (or the equivalent Mexican or Canadian commercial-license requirements). Part 382 also states its own exceptions — among them, employers and drivers who are subject only to a different DOT agency's testing rules (49 CFR Part 655, for certain transit operations), specified military and covered-farm-vehicle drivers a state must or may exempt from the Part 383 licensing requirement, and firefighters operating emergency vehicles under the conditions the regulation states.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "This part applies to service agents and to every person and to all employers of such persons who operate a commercial motor vehicle in commerce in any State and are subject to:
(1) The commercial driver's license requirements of part 383 of this subchapter;
(2) The Licencia Federal de Conductor (Mexico) requirements; or
(3) The commercial drivers license requirements of the Canadian National Safety Code."
  — 49 CFR § 382.103(a) (eCFR text, title 49, current as of Sept. 3, 2026), 49 CFR § 382.103(a) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-03/title-49.xml?part=382&section=382.103)
  Known gap: This clause quotes 49 CFR § 382.103(a) (the general coverage rule) and paraphrases, without independently quoting, the exceptions listed in § 382.103(d) — the exact conditions attached to the military, farm-vehicle, covered-farm-vehicle, and firefighter exceptions are more detailed than this paraphrase states, and this clause does not restate them in full. It does not determine whether a specific position requires a commercial driver's license, involves a vehicle meeting Part 383's licensing thresholds, or otherwise falls within or outside Part 382's coverage — that depends on facts about the vehicle and role this sheet does not address. This is federal law, applicable regardless of state; it is not a claim about any California-specific requirement.

THE CLEARINGHOUSE AND "EMPLOYER," DEFINED
Part 382's own definitions section describes the Clearinghouse as the FMCSA database that Subpart G requires employers and service agents to report information to, and to query, regarding drivers subject to the federal controlled-substance and alcohol testing regulations. The same section defines "employer," for purposes of the whole part, as a person or entity employing one or more employees (including a self-employed individual) that is subject to DOT agency regulations requiring compliance with Part 382 — the entity responsible for overall implementation of the DOT drug and alcohol program requirements — and it separately states that a service agent (a term covering entities such as a consortium/third-party administrator that helps administer a testing program) is not itself an "employer" for the part's purposes.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Commercial Driver's License Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse (Clearinghouse) means the FMCSA database that subpart G of this part requires employers and service agents to report information to and to query regarding drivers who are subject to the DOT controlled substance and alcohol testing regulations."
  — 49 CFR § 382.107 (eCFR text, title 49, current as of Sept. 3, 2026), defining "Commercial Driver's License Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse", 49 CFR § 382.107 (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-03/title-49.xml?part=382&section=382.107)
  "Employer means a person or entity employing one or more employees (including an individual who is self-employed) that is subject to DOT agency regulations requiring compliance with this part. The term, as used in this part, means the entity responsible for overall implementation of DOT drug and alcohol program requirements, including individuals employed by the entity who take personnel actions resulting from violations of this part and any applicable DOT agency regulations. Service agents are not employers for the purposes of this part."
  — 49 CFR § 382.107 (eCFR text, title 49, current as of Sept. 3, 2026), defining "Employer", 49 CFR § 382.107 (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-03/title-49.xml?part=382&section=382.107)
  Known gap: Both quotations below come from the same statutory-note-equivalent section, 49 CFR § 382.107, treated together here as one connected source rather than as independent corroboration of each other. This clause does not restate the balance of § 382.107's lengthy definitions list (covering terms such as "driver," "safety-sensitive function," "actual knowledge," and "refuse to submit," among others), several of which matter to how the query and prohibition rules described in this document's other clauses actually apply; those terms are used in this document's other clauses without being independently defined here. It does not determine whether a specific business meets this definition of "employer" in its own circumstances.

THE PRE-EMPLOYMENT QUERY REQUIREMENT
Federal regulation prohibits an employer from employing a driver, who is subject to the federal controlled-substance and alcohol testing rules, to perform a safety-sensitive function without first conducting a pre-employment query of the Clearinghouse. The query is meant to show whether that driver has a verified positive, adulterated, or substituted controlled-substance test result; an alcohol confirmation test result of 0.04 or higher; a refusal to submit to testing; or an employer's report of actual knowledge of certain alcohol or controlled-substance use. This kind of query is called a "full query" — one that releases the underlying Clearinghouse information to the employer and requires the individual driver's specific consent.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(1) Employers must not employ a driver subject to controlled substances and alcohol testing under this part to perform a safety-sensitive function without first conducting a pre-employment query of the Clearinghouse to obtain information about whether the driver has a verified positive, adulterated, or substituted controlled substances test result; has an alcohol confirmation test with a concentration of 0.04 or higher; has refused to submit to a test in violation of § 382.211; or that an employer has reported actual knowledge, as defined at § 382.107, that the driver used alcohol on duty in violation of § 382.205, used alcohol before duty in violation of § 382.207, used alcohol following an accident in violation of § 382.209, or used a controlled substance, in violation of § 382.213.
(2) The employer must conduct a full query under this section, which releases information in the Clearinghouse to an employer and requires that the individual driver give specific consent."
  — 49 CFR § 382.701(a) (eCFR text, title 49, current as of Sept. 3, 2026), 49 CFR § 382.701(a) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-03/title-49.xml?part=382&section=382.701)
  Known gap: This clause quotes 49 CFR § 382.701(a) only. It does not cover the separate annual query requirement for continuing employees (covered in this document's next clause), the driver-consent mechanics that make a full query possible (also covered separately), or the recordkeeping and prohibition provisions found later in the same section. It does not determine whether a particular driver is subject to controlled substances and alcohol testing under this part, or whether a particular role involves a "safety-sensitive function" as Part 382 defines that term — both threshold questions this clause does not resolve.

DRIVER CONSENT TO A CLEARINGHOUSE QUERY
Federal regulation requires the driver's own consent before an employer may query the Clearinghouse at all. To determine only whether any record exists for a particular driver, the employer must first obtain that driver's written or electronic consent, which the querying employer must retain for three years from the date of the last query. To actually access the substantive information in a driver's Clearinghouse record — a verified positive, adulterated, or substituted test result; a qualifying alcohol confirmation result; a testing refusal; a specified employer report of actual knowledge; or the SAP, return-to-duty, or follow-up-testing records described in the regulation — the driver must separately submit electronic consent through the Clearinghouse itself, granting the employer access to those specific records. The regulation also states the consequence of a refusal: an employer may not permit a driver to perform a safety-sensitive function if that driver refuses to grant the required consent.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "No employer may query the Clearinghouse to determine whether a record exists for any particular driver without first obtaining that driver's written or electronic consent. The employer conducting the search must retain the consent for 3 years from the date of the last query."
  — 49 CFR § 382.703(a) (eCFR text, title 49, current as of Sept. 3, 2026), 49 CFR § 382.703(a) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-03/title-49.xml?part=382&section=382.703)
  "No employer may permit a driver to perform a safety-sensitive function if the driver refuses to grant the consent required by paragraph (a) or (b) of this section."
  — 49 CFR § 382.703(c) (eCFR text, title 49, current as of Sept. 3, 2026), 49 CFR § 382.703(c) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-03/title-49.xml?part=382&section=382.703)
  Known gap: This clause quotes 49 CFR § 382.703(a) through (c) of the same section; they are treated together here as one connected source. It does not cover subdivisions (d) and (e), which describe the mechanics of how a driver's consent is transmitted to FMCSA through the Clearinghouse itself. It does not determine whether any specific driver has given or refused consent, and it does not itself constitute a consent form.

THE ANNUAL QUERY REQUIREMENT FOR CONTINUING DRIVERS
Beyond the pre-employment query, federal regulation requires an employer to query the Clearinghouse at least once per year for every employee subject to the federal controlled-substance and alcohol testing rules, to determine whether Clearinghouse information exists about that employee. In place of a full query, an employer may instead obtain the driver's consent to a "limited query" to satisfy this annual requirement — a query that tells the employer only whether Clearinghouse information about the driver exists, without releasing that information. If a limited query shows that information does exist, the employer must then conduct a full query within 24 hours; if the employer does not do so within that window, the driver may not continue performing any safety-sensitive function until the employer completes the full query and the results confirm the driver's record contains none of the regulation's stated prohibitions.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(1) Employers must conduct a query of the Clearinghouse at least once per year for information for all employees subject to controlled substance and alcohol testing under this part to determine whether information exists in the Clearinghouse about those employees.
(2) In lieu of a full query, as described in paragraph (a)(2) of this section, an employer may obtain the individual driver's consent to conduct a limited query to satisfy the annual query requirement in paragraph (b)(1) of this section. The limited query will tell the employer whether there is information about the individual driver in the Clearinghouse, but will not release that information to the employer. The individual driver may give consent to conduct limited queries that is effective for more than one year.
(3) If the limited query shows that information exists in the Clearinghouse about the individual driver, the employer must conduct a full query, in accordance with paragraph (a)(2) of this section, within 24 hours of conducting the limited query. If the employer fails to conduct a full query within 24 hours, the employer must not allow the driver to continue to perform any safety-sensitive function until the employer conducts the full query and the results confirm that the driver's Clearinghouse record contains no prohibitions as defined in paragraph (d) of this section."
  — 49 CFR § 382.701(b) (eCFR text, title 49, current as of Sept. 3, 2026), 49 CFR § 382.701(b) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-03/title-49.xml?part=382&section=382.701)
  Known gap: This clause quotes 49 CFR § 382.701(b)(1) through (3) — subdivisions of the same section as this document's pre-employment-query clause, treated together with it as one connected source rather than independent corroboration. It does not cover § 382.701(c), the separate 30-day post-query notification duty FMCSA itself owes the employer, which is not an employer obligation and is not restated here. It does not state which specific query method any particular employer has used or will use for any particular driver.

THE PROHIBITION AND ITS RETURN-TO-DUTY EXCEPTION
Federal regulation states a general prohibition: no employer may allow a driver it employs or intends to hire or use to perform any safety-sensitive function if a Clearinghouse query shows a verified positive, adulterated, or substituted controlled-substance test result; a disqualifying alcohol confirmation result; a testing refusal; or a specified employer report of actual knowledge of alcohol or controlled-substance use — except where the query also shows that the driver has completed the SAP (substance abuse professional) evaluation, referral, and education or treatment process, achieved a negative return-to-duty test result, and completed the prescribed follow-up testing plan (or, for a driver still completing follow-up testing, has met the same SAP and return-to-duty conditions while the employer itself assumes responsibility for managing the remaining follow-up testing).

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "No employer may allow a driver the employer employs or intends to hire or use to perform any safety-sensitive function if the results of a Clearinghouse query demonstrate that the driver has a verified positive, adulterated, or substituted controlled substances test result; has an alcohol confirmation test with a concentration of 0.04 or higher; has refused to submit to a test in violation of § 382.211; or that an employer has reported actual knowledge, as defined at § 382.107, that the driver used alcohol on duty in violation of § 382.205, used alcohol before duty in violation of § 382.207, used alcohol following an accident in violation of § 382.209, or used a controlled substance in violation of § 382.213, except where a query of the Clearinghouse demonstrates:
(1) That the driver has successfully completed the SAP evaluation, referral, and education/treatment process set forth in part 40, subpart O, of this title; achieves a negative return-to-duty test result; and completes the follow-up testing plan prescribed by the SAP."
  — 49 CFR § 382.701(d) (eCFR text, title 49, current as of Sept. 3, 2026), 49 CFR § 382.701(d) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-03/title-49.xml?part=382&section=382.701)
  Known gap: This clause quotes 49 CFR § 382.701(d), a single subdivision of the same section as this document's other § 382.701 clauses; it does not independently corroborate them, and they do not independently corroborate it. It does not describe the SAP evaluation and return-to-duty process itself (governed by 49 CFR Part 40, Subpart O), which this clause references only as the regulation itself references it, without independently fetching or verifying Part 40's own text. It does not determine whether any specific Clearinghouse query result falls within this exception.

QUERY RECORDKEEPING
Federal regulation requires an employer to retain, for three years, a record of each Clearinghouse query it makes and all information it receives in response. As of January 6, 2023, the regulation treats an employer's own valid Clearinghouse registration as satisfying this recordkeeping requirement.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Recordkeeping required. Employers must retain for 3 years a record of each query and all information received in response to each query made under this section. As of January 6, 2023, an employer who maintains a valid registration fulfills this requirement."
  — 49 CFR § 382.701(e) (eCFR text, title 49, current as of Sept. 3, 2026), 49 CFR § 382.701(e) (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-03/title-49.xml?part=382&section=382.701)
  Known gap: This clause quotes 49 CFR § 382.701(e) only, the same section as this document's other § 382.701 clauses, treated as one connected source with them rather than independent corroboration. It does not describe how, mechanically, a Clearinghouse registration "fulfills" the recordkeeping requirement, or what an employer's registration record actually contains — the regulation's text quoted here states the rule but not its underlying mechanics. It does not state what records, if any, any particular employer currently retains for any particular driver.

PENALTIES FOR NONCOMPLIANCE
Federal regulation states that an employer or driver who violates any requirement of Part 382 — including the pre-employment and annual query duties, the consent requirements, and the recordkeeping duty described in this document — is subject to the civil and/or criminal penalty provisions of 49 U.S.C. § 521(b). The regulation states the same consequence for a violation of the related testing-procedure rules in 49 CFR Part 40.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Any employer or driver who violates the requirements of this part shall be subject to the civil and/or criminal penalty provisions of 49 U.S.C. 521(b). In addition, any employer or driver who violates the requirements of 49 CFR part 40 shall be subject to the civil and/or criminal penalty provisions of 49 U.S.C. 521(b)."
  — 49 CFR § 382.507 (eCFR text, title 49, current as of Sept. 3, 2026), 49 CFR § 382.507 (https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-09-03/title-49.xml?part=382&section=382.507)
  Known gap: This clause quotes 49 CFR § 382.507 in full; that provision states the penalty consequence by cross-reference to 49 U.S.C. § 521(b) rather than reciting that statute's own penalty amounts or procedure, and this document does not separately fetch or quote 49 U.S.C. § 521(b) itself — the amounts, tiers, and enforcement procedure that statute sets are not stated here. It does not determine whether any violation has occurred or what penalty, if any, would apply in a specific case.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
By signing below, the undersigned acknowledge that this information sheet was provided and that it states general rules of federal law about the Commercial Driver's License Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse rather than advice about Jordan Lee's specific position or Acme Trucking, Inc.'s specific legal obligations.

Employer: Acme Trucking, Inc.
By: _______________
Date: September 6, 2026

Driver / Applicant: Jordan Lee
Position: Commercial Driver
Signature: _______________
Date: September 6, 2026

No employer may allow a driver the employer employs or intends to hire or use to perform any safety-sensitive function if the results of a Clearinghouse query demonstrate that the driver has a verified positive, adulterated, or substituted controlled substances test result; has an alcohol confirmation test with a concentration of 0.04 or higher; has refused to submit to a test in violation of § 382.211; or that an employer has reported actual knowledge, as defined at § 382.107, that the driver used alcohol on duty in violation of § 382.205, used alcohol before duty in violation of § 382.207, used alcohol following an accident in violation of § 382.209, or used a controlled substance in violation of § 382.213, except where a query of the Clearinghouse demonstrates:
(1) That the driver has successfully completed the SAP evaluation, referral, and education/treatment process set forth in part 40, subpart O, of this title; achieves a negative return-to-duty test result; and completes the follow-up testing plan prescribed by the SAP.

expectedJSON.gap: This clause quotes 49 CFR § 382.701(d), a single subdivision of the same section as this document's other § 382.701 clauses; it does not independently corroborate them, and they do not independently corroborate it. It does not describe the SAP evaluation and return-to-duty process itself (governed by 49 CFR Part 40, Subpart O), which this clause references only as the regulation itself references it, without independently fetching or verifying Part 40's own text. It does not determine whether any specific Clearinghouse query result falls within this exception.

expectedJSON.body: Federal regulation requires an employer to retain, for three years, a record of each Clearinghouse query it makes and all information it receives in response. As of January 6, 2023, the regulation treats an employer's own valid Clearinghouse registration as satisfying this recordkeeping requirement.

citations.case: 49 CFR § 382.701(e) (eCFR text, title 49, current as of Sept. 3, 2026)
citations.quote: Recordkeeping required. Employers must retain for 3 years a record of each query and all information received in response to each query made under this section. As of January 6, 2023, an employer who maintains a valid registration fulfills this requirement.

expectedJSON.gap: This clause quotes 49 CFR § 382.701(e) only, the same section as this document's other § 382.701 clauses, treated as one connected source with them rather than independent corroboration. It does not describe how, mechanically, a Clearinghouse registration "fulfills" the recordkeeping requirement, or what an employer's registration record actually contains — the regulation's text quoted here states the rule but not its underlying mechanics. It does not state what records, if any, any particular employer currently retains for any particular driver.

expectedJSON.body: Federal regulation states that an employer or driver who violates any requirement of Part 382 — including the pre-employment and annual query duties, the consent requirements, and the recordkeeping duty described in this document — is subject to the civil and/or criminal penalty provisions of 49 U.S.C. § 521(b). The regulation states the same consequence for a violation of the related testing-procedure rules in 49 CFR Part 40.

citations.case: 49 CFR § 382.507 (eCFR text, title 49, current as of Sept. 3, 2026)
citations.quote: Any employer or driver who violates the requirements of this part shall be subject to the civil and/or criminal penalty provisions of 49 U.S.C. 521(b). In addition, any employer or driver who violates the requirements of 49 CFR part 40 shall be subject to the civil and/or criminal penalty provisions of 49 U.S.C. 521(b).

expectedJSON.gap: This clause quotes 49 CFR § 382.507 in full; that provision states the penalty consequence by cross-reference to 49 U.S.C. § 521(b) rather than reciting that statute's own penalty amounts or procedure, and this document does not separately fetch or quote 49 U.S.C. § 521(b) itself — the amounts, tiers, and enforcement procedure that statute sets are not stated here. It does not determine whether any violation has occurred or what penalty, if any, would apply in a specific case.
